content:
Christian missionaries to Muslims often begin with the Quran. Its verses honour Jesus (peace be upon him) more than most Muslims' neighbours expect, and missionary writers argue that those verses, read closely, point beyond Islam to the Christian faith.[1]

The verses are real, and so are the arguments built on them. The question in each case is what the verse says in its own setting.

This article aims to provide context to those arguments, insha'Allah, in five Quranic passages that Christian writers use, each set beside the verses around it. The Quran's own rule for reading scripture frames them: some "distort the Book with their tongues", so that "you would think it is a part of the Book, but it is no part of the Book" (3:78).[2]

The "Camel Method" asks a Muslim to read the passage on Mary and Jesus in Surah Al ʿImran. Phil Parshall, reviewing its training manual, called it "a key witness technique": "asking a Muslim to read Surah Al-Imran 3:42-55 from the Quran."[3]

The passage honours Mary and calls her son a Word from God and a messenger. Four verses after it ends, the Quran explains his birth: "The similitude of Jesus before Allah is as that of Adam" (3:59).[2] We set out the method and its critics in the Camel Method.

Christian writers read the title beside John 1. Sam Shamoun writes that "God's Word is not part of creation but the means through which God both communicates and brings creation into being."[4]

The Quran explains the title in the same chapter. Mary asks how she can have a son, and the answer is: "When He hath decreed a plan, He but saith to it, 'Be,' and it is!" (3:47).[2] We set out the verses on the title in Jesus as a Word from God.

In the same essay, titled "The Quran Confirms the Trinity!", Shamoun concludes from 4:171 that "the Quran recognizes that Jesus is an eternal Spirit who became flesh". He quotes Gilchrist's observation that the phrase rūḥun minhu, "a spirit from Him", is used "in exactly the same form in Surah 58:22".[4]

Shamoun's conclusion is an error, and the observation he quotes is what proves it. In 58:22 the phrase describes believers: God "has written Faith in their hearts, and strengthened them with a spirit from Himself".[2] If the phrase made Jesus divine, it would make every believer in that verse divine as well. The Quran uses the same language of Adam, into whom God "breathed... of My spirit" (15:29), and the verse of 4:171 itself goes on: "Say not 'Trinity': desist."[2]

Baptist Press reported that the Camel Method uses "selected verses from the Quran" to show that Isa "is holy, has power over death and knows the way to heaven".[5] The Quran does tell of Jesus raising the dead.

Every time, it adds the condition: "thou bringest forth the dead by My leave", God says to him (5:110), and Jesus himself says, "I quicken the dead, by Allah's leave" (3:49).[2] The power over death in these verses is God's, given to His messenger as a sign. The staff of Moses became "a snake, active in motion" (20:20), and no one takes Moses for God.

The Christian site Jesus-Islam argues from 10:94 that Muhammad (peace be upon him), "and thus all Muslims", was "ordained to consider the Bible as the first source of revelation".[6] The verse reads: "If thou wert in doubt as to what We have revealed unto thee, then ask those who have been reading the Book from before thee: the Truth hath indeed come to thee from thy Lord: so be in no wise of those in doubt" (10:94).[2]

The verse names its own conclusion: the truth has come to the Prophet, and he is not to doubt it. The Quran also calls itself the guardian over the scripture before it (5:48), and warns of those who "distort the Book with their tongues" (3:78).[2] We set out the classical readings of the verse in ask those who read the scripture.

The bottom line

Christian missionaries use real verses of the Quran, and they choose them well: the Camel passage of Surah Al ʿImran, the titles "Word" and "spirit from Him", the miracles and the command to ask the People of the Book. In each case the verse around the quotation answers the argument built on it.

Jesus is like Adam, the Word is God's command "Be", the spirit from God is given to believers too, the miracles come "by Allah's leave", and the verse on asking ends by telling the Prophet not to doubt. Read whole, the Quran's verses on Jesus lead where he leads in the Quran: "worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord" (5:72).[2] Allahu alam.

Notes

  1. The sources in notes 3 to 6 document each argument.
  2. Quran 3:47; 3:49; 3:59; 3:78; 4:171; 5:48; 5:72; 5:110; 10:94; 15:29; 20:20; 58:22, translated by A. Yusuf Ali.
  3. Phil Parshall, review of Kevin Greeson, Camel Training Manual (Midlothian, VA: WIGTake, 2004), Evangelical Missions Quarterly, July 2005.
  4. Sam Shamoun, "The Quran Confirms the Trinity! Pt. 3a", answering-islam.org, quoting John Gilchrist, The Titles of Jesus in the Qur'an and the Bible, Christianity and Islam Series no. 5, section 3, "A Spirit from God".
  5. Bob Allen, "Seminary President Labels Mission Strategy 'Heresy'", Associated Baptist Press, 11 February 2010.
  6. Jesus-Islam, "Should the Muslim read the Bible? What does the Koran say?", jesus-islam.org.
